help.title: Help
help.intro: Quick guidance for recording and editing with Openscreen.
help.recordingDescription: Choose a screen or window, enable the inputs you need, then start recording. Your selected microphone, camera, cursor and preview settings are remembered.
help.studioDescription: Open a recording or project to edit zooms, trims, blur regions, playback speed, cursor, camera layout and audio.
help.exportDescription: Export an edited MP4 or GIF, or save an Openscreen project when you want to continue editing later.
help.mcpDescription: Studio MCP {{version}} provides {{count}} local Studio tools. It can edit, preview, save copies and export, but cannot start recording, run shell commands, delete, overwrite or upload files.
help.troubleshootingDescription: If preview or capture is unavailable, reselect the source and confirm screen, microphone and camera permissions in your system settings.

guide.intro: Choose a topic for complete instructions. The first guide covers the full recording workflow.

quickStart.title: Quick start
quickStart.intro: Record, review and save a video in one workflow.
quickStart.step1: Choose a full screen or application window from the source selector.
quickStart.step2: Enable the microphone, system audio, camera, cursor and preview you want in the recording.
quickStart.step3: Press Record. The countdown appears on the selected screen or window before capture starts.
quickStart.step4: Use Pause and Resume without creating a new recording, or Stop when the session is complete.
quickStart.step5: Open Studio, send the video to another editor, or export directly according to Settings.

recording.title: Recording setup and controls
recording.intro: The control bar remains above other windows and remembers your selected modes and devices.
recording.step1: Screen records the complete monitor; Window follows the selected application and its supported popup surfaces.
recording.step2: Microphone and system audio are separate inputs. Choose the exact microphone from its menu and set its level there.
recording.step3: Camera enables the webcam overlay. Camera controls expose settings supported by the selected device.
recording.step4: Cursor mode controls whether the system cursor is burned in or captured as an editable Studio overlay.
recording.step5: Preview shows the selected source, cursor mode and webcam state before and during recording.
recording.step6: Settings controls quiet recording, after-recording behavior and when the control bar hides.

pause.title: Pause, resume and stop
pause.intro: Pause and resume operate on the same synchronized recording session.
pause.step1: Pause stops captured video and audio time together; the paused interval is excluded from the result.
pause.step2: Resume continues the same media tracks and project without inserting the time spent paused.
pause.step3: Stop finalizes the media before applying the selected after-recording action. Long recordings can take time to finalize.
pause.step4: Cancel discards the active session. Use Stop when you need the recording preserved.

studio.title: Open Studio editing
studio.intro: Studio edits a recording non-destructively and keeps the source media separate.
studio.step1: Open a video or .openscreen project. Project files retain timeline edits and references to their media.
studio.step2: Use timeline regions for trims, speed changes, zooms and editable blur effects.
studio.step3: Zoom regions support custom position, size and aspect ratio rather than only fixed presets.
studio.step4: Adjust cursor appearance, webcam layout and microphone mix from their Studio controls.
studio.step5: Preview the current timeline before export and use undo or redo while editing.
studio.step6: Save a project or copy before moving source recordings to another location.

blur.title: Live blur and Studio blur
blur.intro: Live Blurry and editable Studio blur solve different parts of the workflow.
blur.step1: On Windows, the Blur button left of Cursor opens the original Blurry settings panel.
blur.step2: A green Blur button means Blurry is selected. Deselecting it sends Escape to clear the current selection.
blur.step3: Blurry affects the real desktop while recording; the preview reflects what the capture source can see.
blur.step4: Studio blur regions are timeline effects that can be moved, resized or removed after recording.
blur.step5: Blurry is Windows-only. Studio blur remains available for editing on supported desktop platforms.

export.title: Save and export
export.intro: Choose an output based on whether the work is finished or will be edited again.
export.step1: Export MP4 for normal video delivery or GIF for short silent animations.
export.step2: Direct export skips Studio after recording and writes the configured video output immediately.
export.step3: Saving an .openscreen project preserves editable timeline data; it is not a playable video by itself.
export.step4: The after-recording Export action can copy the saved video path to the clipboard.
export.step5: Keep the source recording until the final exported file has been opened and checked.

updates.title: Versions and updates
updates.intro: About shows the installed app, MCP and bundled component versions.
updates.step1: Check for updates is manual and contacts the official wadib/openscreen GitHub release endpoint.
updates.step2: Openscreen never downloads or installs an update without your action.
updates.step3: Capture engines, Blurry and camera controls are compatibility-tested and updated with the app installer.
updates.step4: A release component manifest enables exact per-component comparison; older releases fall back to app version status.

mcp.title: Studio MCP for AI agents
mcp.intro: Studio MCP {{version}} exposes {{count}} local Studio tools through the documented stdio server.
mcp.step1: Agents can inspect status, open a project, review history and save a new project copy.
mcp.step2: Agents can create or adjust zoom, trim, speed, microphone and layout edits through validated arguments.
mcp.step3: Agents can preview, create snapshots and export through Studio's normal media pipeline.
mcp.step4: Agents cannot start recording, run shell commands, delete or overwrite files, upload media or bypass destination checks.

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting and recovery
troubleshooting.intro: Start with the source and permissions, then verify the saved media before changing the project.
troubleshooting.step1: Preview unavailable: reselect the screen or window, then confirm operating-system screen-recording permission.
troubleshooting.step2: Missing microphone or camera: select the device again and confirm microphone or camera permission in system settings.
troubleshooting.step3: No sound in Studio: verify the microphone waveform and selected track, then test an exported MP4 to separate playback from capture issues.
troubleshooting.step4: A long Stop operation can be finalizing the media. Do not terminate Openscreen while the recording is being saved.
troubleshooting.step5: Recordings and projects are retained in Openscreen's application-data recordings folder unless you choose another destination.
troubleshooting.step6: Use Report a problem with the app version, operating system, capture mode and exact error text.
